frameworks.name: Aristotle’s Four Causes & Categories
frameworks.author: Aristotle
frameworks.summary: To understand a thing, ask what it is made of, what shape it has, what made it and what it is for.

concepts.name: Material cause
concepts.summary: What it is made of.

concepts.name: Formal cause
concepts.summary: The shape, pattern or design that makes it this thing.

concepts.name: Efficient cause
concepts.summary: What or who brought it about.

concepts.name: Final cause
concepts.summary: What it is for — its purpose or end.

frameworks.about: Aristotle explained things by asking four kinds of “because”. He also sorted everything that is into categories such as substance, quantity, quality and relation.
frameworks.scope: Understanding any object, event or idea from several sides.
frameworks.limits: Modern science rarely uses final causes for nature; treat purpose as a question, not a proof.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Kant’s Critical Philosophy
frameworks.author: Immanuel Kant
frameworks.summary: What we know is shaped both by the world and by the way our minds take it in.

concepts.name: Sensibility
concepts.summary: We receive things in space and time.

concepts.name: Understanding
concepts.summary: We order what we receive with concepts (the categories).

concepts.name: Reason
concepts.summary: We seek complete answers — and must know its limits.

frameworks.about: Kant asked what we can know, what we ought to do and what we may hope. Knowledge needs both experience and the mind’s own forms.
frameworks.scope: Checking how sure you are and why.
frameworks.limits: A historical theory of knowledge; many later philosophers disagree with parts of it.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Spinoza’s Ethics
frameworks.author: Baruch Spinoza
frameworks.summary: Everything is connected in one nature; understanding the causes of things frees us.

concepts.name: Substance (God or Nature)
concepts.summary: The one whole that everything is part of.

concepts.name: Attributes
concepts.summary: Ways the whole is understood — thought and extension.

concepts.name: Modes
concepts.summary: Particular things: this tree, this thought.

concepts.name: Affects
concepts.summary: Feelings — changes in our power to act.

concepts.name: Conatus
concepts.summary: Each thing’s striving to keep going.

concepts.name: Adequate ideas
concepts.summary: Understanding causes clearly.

concepts.name: Freedom
concepts.summary: Acting from understanding rather than being pushed.

frameworks.about: Spinoza saw one nature expressed in countless things. Seeing how things cause each other turns passive feelings into understanding.
frameworks.scope: Seeing how the things in your life affect each other.
frameworks.limits: A metaphysical system — useful as a way of looking, not a scientific claim.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Hegel’s Dialectic
frameworks.author: G. W. F. Hegel
frameworks.summary: Ideas grow by meeting their opposites and becoming something richer.

concepts.name: Position
concepts.summary: A view as it first appears.

concepts.name: Negation
concepts.summary: What it leaves out or contradicts.

concepts.name: Sublation (Aufhebung)
concepts.summary: A new view that keeps what was true in both.

source.work: Phenomenology of Spirit; Science of Logic

frameworks.about: The triad “thesis–antithesis–synthesis” is a later shorthand; Hegel himself spoke of concepts developing through their own contradictions.
frameworks.scope: Tracing how your views change over time.
frameworks.limits: Real change is messier than three steps.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Heidegger’s Being-in-the-World
frameworks.author: Martin Heidegger
frameworks.summary: We are always already in a world of things, people and projects that matter to us.

concepts.name: Being-in-the-world
concepts.summary: We find ourselves among things we use and care about.

concepts.name: Care (Sorge)
concepts.summary: Things matter to us; we are concerned.

concepts.name: Being-with
concepts.summary: We live alongside others.

concepts.name: Thrownness
concepts.summary: We start from a situation we did not choose.

concepts.name: Projection
concepts.summary: We press ahead into possibilities.

concepts.name: Temporality
concepts.summary: Past, present and future shape each moment.

frameworks.about: Heidegger described human existence from the inside: involved, concerned, finite and open to possibilities.
frameworks.scope: Reflecting on the situations and possibilities of your own life.
frameworks.limits: Dense, contested philosophy; here only as gentle reflection prompts.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Plato’s Divided Line
frameworks.author: Plato
frameworks.summary: Understanding climbs from images, to things, to ideas, to the forms behind them.

concepts.name: Imagination (eikasia)
concepts.summary: Shadows, reflections and copies.

concepts.name: Belief (pistis)
concepts.summary: The physical things we see.

concepts.name: Thought (dianoia)
concepts.summary: Mathematical and reasoned ideas.

concepts.name: Understanding (noesis)
concepts.summary: The forms themselves — the Good.

frameworks.about: With the line and the cave Plato pictures learning as turning from appearances toward what is truly real.
frameworks.scope: Asking how deep your understanding of something goes.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Schopenhauer’s World as Will and Representation
frameworks.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
frameworks.summary: The world is how it appears to us — and beneath that, a restless striving.

concepts.name: Representation
concepts.summary: The world as it shows up to a subject.

concepts.name: Will
concepts.summary: The blind striving behind all appearances.

concepts.name: Art
concepts.summary: Moments of calm contemplation.

concepts.name: Compassion
concepts.summary: Feeling another’s suffering as one’s own.

source.work: The World as Will and Representation

frameworks.about: Schopenhauer joined Kant’s idea of appearances with a dark picture of endless wanting, softened by art and compassion.
frameworks.scope: Noticing wants, appearances and what calms them.
frameworks.limits: A pessimistic outlook; use as one lens among many.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Nietzsche’s Three Metamorphoses
frameworks.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
frameworks.summary: The spirit becomes a camel that carries, a lion that refuses, and a child that creates.

concepts.name: Camel
concepts.summary: Carrying duties and inherited values.

concepts.name: Lion
concepts.summary: Saying no — winning freedom.

concepts.name: Child
concepts.summary: A new beginning — saying yes and creating values.

frameworks.about: A parable about growing from obedience, through rebellion, to creative affirmation.
frameworks.scope: Reflecting on stages of personal growth.
frameworks.limits: Poetic and open to many readings.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Bacon’s Division of Learning
frameworks.author: Francis Bacon
frameworks.summary: All learning comes from three powers of the mind: memory, imagination and reason.

concepts.name: Memory → History
concepts.summary: What happened: natural and civil history.

concepts.name: Imagination → Poetry
concepts.summary: What could be: stories and images.

concepts.name: Reason → Philosophy
concepts.summary: Why it is so: knowledge of God, nature and humans.

frameworks.about: Bacon mapped all knowledge onto the mind’s faculties; the Encyclopédie later borrowed the plan.
frameworks.scope: Sorting what you know by how you came to know it.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Stoicism
frameworks.author: Zeno, Epictetus, Seneca, Marcus Aurelius
frameworks.summary: Tell apart what is up to you from what is not, and practise the virtues.

concepts.name: Up to me
concepts.summary: My judgments, choices and actions.

concepts.name: Not up to me
concepts.summary: Other people, events, reputation, the body’s fortunes.

concepts.name: Wisdom
concepts.summary: Seeing things as they are.

concepts.name: Courage
concepts.summary: Doing right when it is hard.

concepts.name: Justice
concepts.summary: Treating others fairly.

concepts.name: Temperance
concepts.summary: Moderation and self-command.

frameworks.about: A school of practical philosophy about steady judgment and virtue.
frameworks.scope: Sorting worries into what you can and cannot change.
frameworks.limits: Not a substitute for help with serious distress.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Confucian Life — the Great Learning
frameworks.author: Confucian tradition
frameworks.summary: Order in the world grows outward from a cultivated person.
frameworks.about: Eight linked steps: learning and self-cultivation come first; family, community and the wider world follow.
frameworks.scope: Seeing how personal growth reaches family and community.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Existential Life
frameworks.author: Kierkegaard, Sartre, de Beauvoir, Camus
frameworks.summary: We make our lives meaningful through free, responsible choices.

concepts.name: Freedom
concepts.summary: We choose, even when we would rather not.

concepts.name: Responsibility
concepts.summary: Our choices are ours to own.

concepts.name: Authenticity
concepts.summary: Living by what we truly value.

concepts.name: Meaning
concepts.summary: Purpose is made, not handed to us.

concepts.name: Others
concepts.summary: Our freedom is lived among other free people.

frameworks.about: A family of thinkers focused on lived experience, choice and meaning.
frameworks.scope: Reflecting on the choices that shape your life.
frameworks.limits: Reflection only — no countdowns or fear; skip anything you like.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Taoist Life
frameworks.author: Laozi, Zhuangzi
frameworks.summary: Live in harmony with the natural way of things; effortless action, simplicity and balance.

concepts.name: Tao (the Way)
concepts.summary: The source and flow of all things.

concepts.name: De (virtue/power)
concepts.summary: The quiet power of living in accord with the Way.

concepts.name: Wu wei
concepts.summary: Acting without forcing.

concepts.name: Ziran
concepts.summary: Naturalness — being so of itself.

concepts.name: Yin and yang
concepts.summary: Complementary opposites in balance.

concepts.name: Simplicity (pu)
concepts.summary: The uncarved block.

frameworks.about: Classical Chinese thought about flowing with nature rather than against it.
frameworks.scope: Noticing where you push and where you could flow.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.
